title: Backcasting Human-in-the-Loop Triage: Can a Cheap Monitor Produce Audit Summaries That Speed Human Catch Rate?

original_idea.body: On APPS clean/backdoored solutions, have participants classify with vs without a monitor's highlighted-suspicious-region summary, measuring accuracy and time-per-item.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Whether monitor summaries speed human catch rate addresses the HITL audit-budget bottleneck.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Small human study with peers; manageable but coordination adds effort.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused with/without-summary comparison; small-N human study is one dependency.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: HITL UX is neglected by labs, lab-independent, public data.

low_compute.reasoning: Minimal inference for summaries; human study compute-free.

novelty.reasoning: Some 2026 HITL-UX studies exist; the monitor-summary triage angle may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: HITL monitor-aid studies emerging; this summary-triage variant may be open.
